item.content:encoded:
Karachi’s unchecked urbanisation fuels heat water, infrastructure crisis Karachi’s built-up area has expanded by nearly 32 per cent between 2010 and 2025, surpassing 1,400 square kilometres, as agricultural land, grazing areas and open spaces continue to disappear under concrete development, intensifying concerns over Pakistan’s urban planning failures, as reported by The Express Tribune. ANI | Updated: 22-10-2026 14:19 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 14:19 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Karachi’s built-up area has expanded by nearly 32 per cent between 2010 and 2025, surpassing 1,400 square kilometres, as agricultural land, grazing areas and open spaces continue to disappear under concrete development, intensifying concerns over Pakistan’s urban planning failures, as reported by The Express Tribune. According to The Express Tribune, citing an official note from the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO), satellite-based analysis shows that rapid urbanisation has transformed Karachi’s surrounding landscape, increasing pressure on natural resources and essential infrastructure. SUPARCO stated that the growing spread of buildings and paved surfaces is worsening the urban heat island effect, reducing natural water absorption and potentially increasing the risk of flooding during heavy monsoon rainfall. The consequences could include declining labour productivity, rising healthcare costs and greater pressure on electricity, water and drainage networks. Urban planner M Toheed, associated with the Institute of Business Administration (IBA), said Karachi had lost around 40 per cent of its green cover over the past 15 years, while its built-up footprint continued to grow. The estimate requires further verification through comparable land-cover data. Toheed stated that the expanding concrete landscape was creating serious consequences for residents. Reduced vegetation and shade, combined with humid weather, make it harder for the human body to regulate temperature, increasing the risk of heat-related illness. The economic burden also extends to workers facing reduced productivity and households struggling with higher cooling costs. Toheed said Karachi’s population growth had outpaced infrastructure development. He cited prolonged electricity outages in areas including North Karachi and Lyari, with interruptions reportedly reaching 18 hours on Baba Bhit Island. Unreliable electricity and water supplies leave residents with fewer ways to cope with extreme temperatures, while disrupting businesses and daily activities, as cited by The Express Tribune. SUPARCO also linked the loss of natural drainage capacity to greater flood vulnerability, highlighting Karachi’s devastating 2020 floods as an example of the consequences of intense rainfall and inadequate drainage, as reported by The Express Tribune. (ANI)

item.title: Hormuz war risk pushes crude shipping costs sevenfold, squeezes refiners’ margins: Goldman Sachs
item.description: War-related risks in the Strait of Hormuz and an increase in ship-to-ship transfers account for more than half of the USD 20 per barrel year-on-year rise in global crude oil freight rates, according ...
item.content:encoded:
Hormuz war risk pushes crude shipping costs sevenfold, squeezes refiners’ margins: Goldman Sachs War-related risks in the Strait of Hormuz and an increase in ship-to-ship transfers account for more than half of the USD 20 per barrel year-on-year rise in global crude oil freight rates, according to a report by Goldman Sachs (GS). ANI | Updated: 22-10-2026 13:33 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 13:33 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

War-related risks in the Strait of Hormuz and an increase in ship-to-ship transfers account for more than half of the USD 20 per barrel year-on-year rise in global crude oil freight rates, according to a report by Goldman Sachs (GS). The surge in shipping costs is putting pressure on refiners, particularly in Asia, which rely heavily on crude oil imports from distant suppliers. These refiners may have to pass on the higher costs to consumers or accept lower profit margins. Brent crude crossed USD 110 per barrel this week and was trading at around USD 111.51 per barrel at the time of reporting. Another crude oil benchmark was trading at around USD 99.31 per barrel. Goldman Sachs said global crude oil shipping costs are now seven times higher than a year ago. The report noted, “The global average crude freight rate surged above USD 20/bbl from USD 3/bbl a year ago.” The increase in freight rates initially began in the very large crude carrier (VLCC) segment and on Middle Eastern routes but has since spread to all major crude trading routes, with long-distance voyages particularly affected.While most crude oil benchmarks do not directly include transportation costs, higher freight rates can affect refiners' profitability and influence their choice of suppliers. According to GS, “high freight rates may reduce refiners margin’ overall demand for crude and/or skew it towards more closely located crude supplier.” The report identified five key factors behind the USD 20 per barrel year-on-year increase in average global crude freight rates. These include a USD 7 per barrel war risk premium for crossing the Strait of Hormuz, USD 4 from ship-to-ship transfers outside the Persian Gulf, USD 4 from higher maritime fuel prices, USD 3 from inefficient tanker allocation and increased vessel diversions, and USD 2 from restrictions on the Iranian tanker fleet. The report said these factors “will likely continue to support global freight rates as long as the conflict on the Middle East persists.” Goldman Sachs said refiners that depend on crude imports from distant suppliers, particularly in Asia, face higher costs.“Refiners with greater dependence on imported crude from distant suppliers (e.g., refiners in Asia) would have to either pass higher freight costs on to final consumers or accept lower net refinery margins,” the report said. However, passing on these costs to consumers could be difficult in markets where alternatives to oil, such as electric vehicles in China, are widely available, or where retail fuel prices are regulated. The rise in freight costs has put particular pressure on Asian refiners' profit margins. This could lead to lower refined fuel output and push up global fuel prices. Meanwhile, crude oil producers that depend on distant buyers may have to offer steeper discounts to maintain demand. In contrast, suppliers located closer to major consumption centres could benefit from a shift in demand. The report said producers serving distant markets may need to “discount” their crude more heavily, while crude from more centrally located suppliers, such as Brent in north-western Europe and ESPO in Russia, “may gain from some demand reallocation.” Goldman Sachs also highlighted the impact of higher tanker operating costs, driven by rising crew salaries and bunker fuel prices. The report estimated that “global maritime fuel oil prices have increased by nearly $50/bbl, or 70% yoy amid weak exports from the Persian Gulf and Russia and resilient bunker demand from tankers and container ships.” (ANI)

item.title: Balochistan killings raise questions over Pakistan’s record on enforced disappearances

item.content:encoded:
Balochistan killings raise questions over Pakistan’s record on enforced disappearances The bodies of two men previously reported missing after their alleged detention by Pakistani security forces have been discovered in Balochistan’s Kech district, while another family has renewed its demand for justice over a disappearance dating back to 2015, as reported by The Balochistan Post. ANI | Updated: 22-10-2026 12:29 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 12:29 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The bodies of two men previously reported missing after their alleged detention by Pakistani security forces have been discovered in Balochistan’s Kech district, while another family has renewed its demand for justice over a disappearance dating back to 2015, as reported by The Balochistan Post. According to The Balochistan Post, the bodies were recovered from the Saloi Kaur area of Buleda and identified as Yasir and Mehran. Reports said both victims bore signs of torture, raising fresh concerns over alleged custodial killings in the region. Paank, the human rights wing of the Baloch National Movement, condemned the deaths and called for an independent investigation. The organisation said Yasir, a 19-year-old student from Minaz, Buleda, was allegedly taken from his home by Frontier Corps personnel on March 2, 2026. Mehran was reportedly detained during a raid on his residence on November 16, 2025, and transferred to a military camp, the organisation said. Paank called for accountability and an investigation into the alleged involvement of security personnel. Meanwhile, the Voice for Baloch Missing Persons (VBMP) continued its protest outside the Quetta Press Club for the 6,394th consecutive day on Tuesday. Relatives of Abdul Rehman Marri joined the demonstration, seeking information about his whereabouts and demanding his safe recovery. According to his family, Marri was forcibly disappeared from New Kahan in Quetta’s Hazarganji area on January 13, 2015. They said he had never been presented before a court and that they had received no information about his fate. The family appealed to senior authorities to intervene, as highlighted by The Balochistan Post. VBMP chairman Nasrullah Baloch urged the authorities to recover Marri and other missing individuals, stressing that anyone accused of a crime must be produced before a court and dealt with under the law, as reported by The Balochistan Post. (ANI)

item.title: Cricket Australia suspends Megan Schutt for breaching prescription medication use requirements
item.description: Schutt received the ban from Cricket Australia for failing to adhere to requirements around the use of prescription medication, with the veteran right-armer to also miss the opening game of the ...
item.content:encoded:
Cricket Australia suspends Megan Schutt for breaching prescription medication use requirements  Schutt received the ban from Cricket Australia for failing to adhere to requirements around the use of prescription medication, with the veteran right-armer to also miss the opening game of the domestic Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) season as part of her suspension, as per the ICC. ANI | Updated: 22-10-2026 11:52 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 11:52 IST

Megan Schutt. (Photo: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

In a massive blow, Australian pacer Megan Schutt has been ruled out of the final of the three-match series against New Zealand at home after receiving a two-match ban for medication use by Cricket Australia. Schutt received the ban from Cricket Australia for failing to adhere to requirements around the use of prescription medication, with the veteran right-armer to also miss the opening game of the domestic Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) season as part of her suspension, as per the ICC. "Australian player Megan Schutt has been suspended for two matches," Cricket Australia confirmed via a statement as quoted by the ICC. "The breach was a failure to adhere to requirements under the Sports Science and Sports Medicine guidelines with regard to prescription medication. This relates to a single incidence which occurred while out of competition and was not for performance enhancing purposes," the statement added. "The two-match ban includes all international and domestic cricket. We will continue to provide appropriate support to Megan and reinforce the standards and responsibilities expected of everyone representing our game," the statement continued. Schutt accepted the ban immediately and released her own statement to confirm. "I fully accept the penalty handed down and apologise for failing to meet the standards expected of me," Schutt said. I am sorry for the attention this has caused and appreciate the support I have received. While this occurred out of competition and was not performance related, I understand that I am responsible for following the Sports Science and Sports Medicine Guidelines, which players receive regular education on, and I should have adhered to these guidelines," she added. Australia currently lead the three-match T20I series against New Zealand 2-0 and will be looking to complete a series sweep in Sydney on Thursday. While Schutt has yet to take part in the T20I series, the 33-year-old was in good form during the recent ODI series with Bangladesh as part of the ongoing ICC Women's Championship as she collected 10 wickets across the three games. (ANI)
